MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Three-month history of nontraumatic left posterior knee pain. Ultrasound suggests medial meniscal tear. Assess for internal derangement   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is splitting of the fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament unassociated with thickening or deficiency. The finding is favored to represent a described but rare anatomic variant. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint appears to be reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. Involving the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus there is some contour flattening of the inferior margin of the meniscus peripherally suggesting possible deficiency of a portion of the meniscotibial ligamentous attachment. There is no evidence of a significant medial meniscal tear. Articular cartilage of the medial compartment is reasonably well-maintained. There is fraying seen to the posterior surface of the weightbearing surface of medial femoral condyle consistent with moderate focal chondrosis.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. Fibers appear mildly attenuated compatible with a remote partial-thickness sprain. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Projecting in the intercondylar notch surrounding the anterior cruciate ligament, situated anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament there is a multiloculated ganglion cyst measuring about 1.9 cm in length and 1.5 x 1.3 cm in short axis. The finding is consistent with an anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

The medial collateral ligament is intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no evidence of a significant Baker's cyst. A small 8 x 4 mm ganglion cyst is seen projecting posterior to the proximal tendon fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment associated with contour flattening of the inferior surface of the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus. This finding is equivocal but could indicate presence of partial deficiency of the meniscotibial attachment in this region. No discrete medial meniscal tear is identified.

Mild attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with remote partial thickness injury. Associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

Suspected congenital duplication of the medial patellar retinaculum.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Artrosis leve. Quiste de Baker.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento de baja señal del
componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de los componentes sin
alteraciones.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios que de rotura.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial medial y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial de la faceta lateral.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano y de la inserción distal del tendón
cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas , profundo a los tendones de la pata de ganso.
Impresión:
Leve engrosamiento secuelar del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial de la faceta lateral.
Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula.

Probable laminar bursitis profunda a los tendones de la pata de ganso

Findings:  The clinically palpable lump along the medial aspect of the knee is seen to represent a well-circumscribed intra-articular structure measuring 5 x 19 x 19 mm. It is of intermediate low signal intensity on PD fat sat and intermediate low signal intensity on T1 but no associated enhancement post contrast administration. The lesion looks like a loose intra-articular body.  
There is no significant knee effusion. Undersurface fraying of the body of medial meniscus is noted. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Normal tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage. No evidence of osteochondral defect identified to suggest as origin of the described loose intra-articular body.  
Conclusion: 19 mm loose intra-articular body within the anteromedial recess of the knee. Its nature is uncertain. Mild fraying of the undersurface of the medial meniscal body also noted.

Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Patella normal yerleşimlidir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Eklemde mesafesinde ve suprapatellar bursada artmış efüzyon izlenmiştir. Interprétation : 

Il n’y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire ni kyste de Baker significatif avec un liséré de liquide. 

Il y a une formation kystique multilobulé au versant postéro-interne du genou s’étendant à la fois à la bourse du semi-membraneux et à la région intercondylienne postérieure mesurant environ 0,9 x 4,2 x 2,1 cm de diamètre AP, transverse et CC. Il y a un émoussement vertical à la périphérie de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne, de signal moindre par rapport au liquide, qui pourrait être en lien avec une ancienne déchirure longitudinale verticale à la jonction capsulo-méniscale/lésion de type « ramp ». Cette formation kystique pourrait être en lien avec un kyste paraméniscal dans ce contexte ou un kyste paraganglionnaire.

Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial interne, sans atteinte transfixiante ni changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé, à l'exception d'un minime œdème sous-chondral au versant tibial.

Le ménisque externe et le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Les surfaces cartilagineuses fémorotibiales externes sont relativement préservées. 

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure. 

L’alignement patellofémoral demeure dans les limites de la normale. Il y a un foyer d’œdème au sein de la graisse de Hoffa supéro-externe suggérant un syndrome d’accrochage entre le tendon patellaire et le condyle fémoral externe (« Hoffa fat pad impingement »). Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patellofémoral, sans atteinte transfixiante. 

Il y a un petit enthésophyte à l’insertion distale du tendon du quadriceps avec un minime œdème réactionnel associé. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts et sans déchirure. Il n'y a pas de bursite prérotulienne ni infrapatellaire significative notée.

Conclusion :

Il y a un léger émoussement vertical à la périphérie de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne qui pourrait être en lien avec une ancienne déchirure longitudinale verticale à la jonction capsulo-méniscale/lésion de type « ramp. » Il y a une formation kystique multilobulée postéro-interne en lien soit avec un kyste paraméniscal dans ce contexte ou un kyste ganglionnaire.

Il y a un léger œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un accrochage entre le tendon patellaire et le condyle fémoral externe (« Hoffa fat pad impingement »). Ceci pourrait être une cause de douleur périrotulienne. Il y a un léger enthésophyte à l’insertion distale du tendon du quadriceps sans déchirure. 

Il y a une légère chondropathie patellofémorale et fémorotibiale interne.

Il n'y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. 

Il n'y a pas de fracture.

Findings: No significant knee effusion. There is a horizontal tear of the body of the lateral meniscus with early para meniscal cyst formation. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.   The normal tibiofemoral and trochlear articular cartilage. Focal fissuring of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted with underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Lateral meniscal tear with early para meniscal cyst formation. Medial patellar chondromalacia. No ligamentous injury.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Dog pulled patient and left knee twisted.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Degenerative signal within the posterior horn and body junction of medial meniscus without definite tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage thinning and fraying along the medial weightbearing surfaces.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade fissures along the lateral more than medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 MCL sprain.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with low-grade interstitial tearing.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 4 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Grade 1 MCL sprain.
2.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with low-grade interstitial tearing.
3.	Patellofemoral and medial compartment chondrosis. 
4.	Degenerative signal within the posterior horn and body junction of medial meniscus without definite tear.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] [Gender] with right knee pain giving way for one year worse going up and down stairs. No history of injury. Physiotherapy feels instability. Please assess for ligament damage.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is mild thickening and increased T2 signal in the proximal fibers of the patellar tendon consistent with mild patellar tendinosis. There is also mild prepatellar edema consistent with prepatellar bursitis.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates severe chondral fraying with some regions of focal cartilage loss seen to the lateral facet and apex of the patella. These changes are associated with subcortical cyst formation and edema seen to the patella involving lateral facet and apex.
The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea is reasonably well-maintained apart from mild fissuring seen at the medial femoral trochlear articular surface.

The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea also demonstrates focal chondral fissuring at the trochlear apex with subcortical interosseous cyst formation also seen to the femoral trochlea.

No significant osteophytes are seen to the patellofemoral joint.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained overall.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact and appear unremarkable.

There is no evidence of significant Baker's cyst or knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION: 

There is severe articular chondrosis of the patellofemoral joint associated with early evolving degenerative change in the patellofemoral joint compartment.

There is no evidence of internal derangement.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. Myxoid degeneration of the body of medial meniscus is noted but no definite tear. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Normal tibiofemoral articular cartilage. Mild fraying of the lateral patellar facet articular cartilage is noted. The patellofemoral articular cartilage is otherwise well maintained. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Myxoid degeneration of the medial meniscal body but no definite tear.
